Among some of his squad during this period were Andrew North, Mark Sinclair and John Gladwin, who claims his first run for Belgrave was with Brian.
We are reminded of the occasion when our own 1 mile club record holder John Gladwin met Sir Roger Bannister at a function. John introduced himself and they got talking.

Having erased two of John Gladwin’s famous club bests from our record books, Kris doesn’t have to prove himself to Belgravians but his name is obviously still unfamiliar to the announcer at Parliament Hill who reeled off the names of the contenders as they completed the first lap but referred to Kri…
We haven’t previously had a Junior indoor mile listed in our records – so Kris clears that up – and he is only 2 seconds away from John Gladwin’s outdoor Junior mark of 4:09.5.
Kris Gauson may be 18 but he has some extraordinary racing times behind him, having in his two years of membership already relieved John Gladwin of his Youth club records for 800m and 1500m.

John Gladwin placed 2nd in the Surrey County Junior CC (leading Belgrave to a team win) – and won our club 7 ½ miles championship – but he was also troubled by injury and spent some time riding a bike to keep fit.
That record is held by Stuart Paton – and the one mile mark of 4:09.05 held by John Gladwin is sure to go next time Kris runs that distance.

An excellent meal was prepared by Chef Warren Caswell (one-time Belgrave high jumper) and those present ranged from the ageless Bill Lucas (who acted as toastmaster), runners from the 80s and 90s (John Gladwin, Mark Sinclair, Gerry Adams) through to a few from today’s teams.

In the final match John Gladwin led the team home. The Surrey Junior championship was won by Stu Paton from David North, John Gladwin and Paul Richley taking the first four places and the Club took the team title for the third year in succession.
